2.3.name: barrelSync fires macros with zero lifecycle wiring

3.1.name: Migrate enemy + boss payloads to bare invoke

summary.failures: None introduced. Baseline failure set unchanged: top-level 10 failing files, attack dir 6 failing files (identical lists before/after). The pre-existing 'contact detonates exactly once' failure in throwEnemy.test.js exists at baseline too.
summary.decisions: Did not migrate bodyExplosion's payloadHandle storage — it is event-waiting state inside a macro, not an enemy/boss hand-stepping an attack handle. Did not touch theater sandbox stepping (out of scope for this task; M3 TODOs cover it).
summary.tradeoffs: throwEnemy.test.js TTL test became async and imports lifecycle.js dynamically to avoid a new top-level import; test now depends on registry internals (_live) which is consistent with attackLifecycle.test.js conventions.
summary.done: explosiveMonkey.detonate is now a bare fire-and-forget invoke() — _payloadHandle field and its assignment removed; the AttackLifecycle registry (auto-registration in engine.invoke) steps/draws/prunes the explosion/shockwave payload. Updated throwEnemy.test.js: the TTL test now asserts the shockwave lands in AttackLifecycle._live, that no handle is stored on the enemy, and that driving ONLY via AttackLifecycle.stepAll ticks ring-pass damage over the duration (proves the previously inert shockwave now works). Scanned petal-panic/js/enemies + js/boss for other stored-handle/manual-step patterns: explosiveMonkey was the only one (bodyExplosion macro stores h.state.payloadHandle but uses it to wait/forward events, not to hand-step — left as-is).
summary.lessons_learned: The old _payloadHandle was never read anywhere except the test — confirming the latent unstepped-shockwave bug. Shockwave ring-pass requires the victim distance to be > startRadius (4px) and <= current radius on some tick; place victims ~30px out for deterministic single-tick capture.
